A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoCoIns work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures that support reliable matching. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–5, plus human, animal and multi-subject examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds FID evaluation, loss and hyperparameter comparisons, latent-space analyses and generated examples.

M1.justification: The mapping network, pseudo-word insertion, frozen generator, masked contrastive loss, background preservation and negative-distance weighting schedule remain unchanged. Appendix B discloses implementation choices; the DreamSim variant in Appendix C is an ablation rather than a replacement method.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds training and generation with LSUN car images, extending v1's human and cat/dog coverage. CelebA, Portraits, Scenes and the two-person generation scenario are retained.

E2.justification: v1's multi-subject Figure 6 shows only CoCoIns; v2's additional Figure 12 compares it with Consistory and StoryDiffusion in that setting. Comparator membership in the original Portraits and Scenes experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The original 1K-prompt Portraits and Scenes protocols remain intact. Appendix C adds FID evaluation using 10K images from Scenes repeated ten times, with each method's own base generator as reference, plus fixed-noise latent analyses using 100 codes. Appendix D adds a 100-image segmentation audit. These supplement the original evaluation.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 compares MSE and DreamSim losses, tests sensitivity to background weight and negative-distance schedule parameters, and examines latent interpolation and pseudo-word neighbors (Tables 9–12; Figures 8–9). The segmentation audit adds another diagnostic check, substantially broadening analysis of the method.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new random-code and segmentation samples are evaluation designs, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical values. New Table 8 reports FID values of 9.2 for CoCoIns, 13.3 for Consistory and 15.2 for StoryDiffusion, each against its own base model. Tables 9–12 and Figures 8–13 add loss comparisons, sensitivity findings, latent-space behavior and generation results, substantially expanding the evidence without changing the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, the masked-distance construction and weighting schedule remain mathematically equivalent. The appendices add empirical and explanatory material, without new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: independent subject-consistent generation without subject-specific tuning or reference images, contrastive pseudo-word learning, and potential extensions beyond single human subjects. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendices C–E substantially expand interpretation: they explain the preference for MSE over perceptual losses, interpret interpolation and neighbor results as meaningful identity structure, and discuss hyperparameter tradeoffs. They also qualify segmentation reliability by the clean portrait setting and explicitly identify thorough multi-subject evaluation as future work.

D1.justification: Appendices B and D supply previously unspecified architecture and training settings, including an eight-layer MLP, 256-dimensional codes and 5,000 steps, plus hardware/runtime, filtering, LLM prompts and licensing information. The abstract now reports code and weights as available. Conversely, v2 omits v1's explicit description of fine-tuning the face-trained model on 10K cat/dog images.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to LSUN and Prompt-to-Prompt and expands the comparison of approach categories in Appendix A/Table 6. The main related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain unchanged; bibliographic corrections and citation-style changes are presentational.

P1.justification: v2 polishes the main prose, standardizes terminology such as 'generations,' updates the title/front matter and reverses the order of the extension paragraphs. Appendices A–F organize additional explanations, while the original main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document switches from two columns to a single-column TMLR layout, with extensively reformatted tables, captions and figure placement. The original multi-subject and general-concept figures exchange numbers, the latter gains a car row, and Tables 6–12 and Figures 8–13 introduce substantial new displays.

improvement.justification: Appendices B and D address important reproducibility gaps by specifying the training configuration and data preparation. The added loss, sensitivity and latent-space analyses substantially strengthen support for design choices while preserving the original results. These gains outweigh the reduced specificity of animal fine-tuning details. Uncertainty reporting remains absent, and the new FID evidence measures proximity to each method's own base distribution rather than quality against a common reference.
